exposure: cervical dilatation at the time of emergent cesarean section (4-9 cm vs. 10 cm)
cohort: 577 patients who underwent emergent cesarean sections at 4 cm or more of cervical dilatation.
finding: Emergent cesarean sections performed at complete cervical dilatation are associated with increased intra-operative and post-operative maternal complications compared to those performed during active labor (4-9 cm dilatation).
mod_finding: Emergent cesarean sections at complete cervical dilatation are linked to higher rates of maternal uterine atony, uterine incision extension, longer hospital stays, and increased infection-related readmissions compared to those performed at earlier stages of active labor.
